external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A library member who uses the library app to borrow, renew and reserve books.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who manually extend loans, clear account blocks and mark books returned.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand

processes.name: library app
processes.description: The app on a member's phone used to borrow, renew and reserve books.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

processes.name: self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where members scan their library card and books being borrowed or returned.
processes.source_excerpt: Every branch has self-service kiosks where a member scans their library card and the books they are borrowing or returning.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: The REST service that is the only component stated to read or write loans and that handles lending operations.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: Exposure claims conflict across sources. Lending service note: "The lending API is internal-only." Interview transcript: "The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet." Authentication is unverified: Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in," and could not say what it accepts or does with rejected calls.

processes.name: circulation page
processes.description: The circulation page served by the lending API through which desk staff perform manual account and loan actions.
processes.source_excerpt: someone at the desk opens the circulation page and marks it returned, or clears the block on the account.
processes.notes: The page is described as served by the lending API; its independent implementation is not stated.

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: The single database containing members, loans, reservations, names, email addresses, home addresses and full borrowing histories.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: The interview corrects the earlier statement about two databases: "We merged those in the spring. It's one loans database now. The old reservations database is gone."

data_flows.name: manage loans
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to borrow, renew or reserve books.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.

data_flows.name: change loans
data_flows.description: The library app calls the lending API for borrowing, renewal and reservation actions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member, and the API checks the loan rules and writes the change.
data_flows.data_description: Member, book, loan renewal, borrowing and reservation requests

data_flows.name: send loans
data_flows.description: A kiosk sends a loan record to the lending API when a book is borrowed.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.notes: The interview does not establish whether kiosks communicate directly with the loans database; it states only that the API receives what arrives from them.
data_flows.data_description: Loan records including the member and borrowed books

data_flows.name: send returns
data_flows.description: A kiosk sends a return record to the lending API when a book is returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.notes: The interview does not establish whether kiosks communicate directly with the loans database; it states only that the API receives what arrives from them.
data_flows.data_description: Return records including the member and returned books

data_flows.name: manage records
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page to extend loans, clear account blocks and mark books returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand, through a circulation page the lending API serves.
data_flows.notes: All desk staff use the same shared login; the password is taped under the desk.

data_flows.name: read-write loans
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes the loans database while checking rules and recording changes.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.data_description: Members, loans, reservations and borrowing history

trust_boundaries.name: member phones
trust_boundaries.description: Phones used by members to run the library app; the phones are outside the library's stated system control.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network on which branch kiosks and desk staff work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data-centre zone where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

assumptions.assumption: The member phones form a tenant trust boundary because they are members' own devices outside the library's stated control.
assumptions.basis: The source places the library app on members' phones; the trust-boundary definition classifies a customer's own device as tenant-controlled.

assumptions.assumption: The lending API presents a web interface because the source identifies it as a REST API.
assumptions.basis: The source states, "It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out." The interface-kind definition classifies REST APIs as web.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database contains names, email addresses, home addresses and full member borrowing histories, whose disclosure harms people.
